statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-40356: in MIT krb5 1.18 and later, if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a NegoEx message with a short header length that causes an integer underflow in parse_message() and a read overrun of up to 52 bytes, possibly terminating the process. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3 (https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html; commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2e75f0d9362fb979f5fc92829431a590a130929f, on the 1.22 branch https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/acea6182e46fff3d1d64a3172cdff307b07ca441). Alpine lists it under 1.22.3-r0 in the 3.23-stable main/krb5 APKBUILD secfixes (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/krb5/APKBUILD). This owner's published builds for Alpine 3.23 are 1.22.1-r0 and 1.22.3-r0. The NegoEx code is in libgssapi_krb5, shipped in the krb5-libs package: in 1.22.3-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64, libkrb5 reports krb5-1.22.3-final; in 1.22.1-r0 it reports krb5-1.22.1-final, an MIT release without the fix. The range ends at 1.22.3-r0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-40356: in MIT krb5 1.18 and later, if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a NegoEx message with a short header length that causes an integer underflow in parse_message() and a read overrun of up to 52 bytes, possibly terminating the process. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3 (https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html; commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2e75f0d9362fb979f5fc92829431a590a130929f). Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 (DSA-6293-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-40356). The DHI krb5 package for Debian 13 is built from Debian's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 source, which carries that fix, and the DHI Debian repository publishes three rebuilds of it. The NegoEx code is in libgssapi-krb5-2. We checked libgssapi-krb5-2 in all three published rebuilds for amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum: libgssapi_krb5.so.2.2 is byte-identical across the three rebuilds on each architecture. The debug information for it in libkrb5-dbg maps machine code in negoex_parse_token, into which parse_message() is inlined, to line 399 of negoex_util.c at the columns of the header_len < (size_t)(in->ptr - msg_base) comparison, the short-header check this fix adds; in the unfixed source that line is a different statement. The package changelog also records the fix for CVE-2026-40356. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at the first published rebuild.
